title: ID0362414-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P9 170001020] TF2 exploded
description:
Reported behavior/issue:
When our service partner was going to do the service they found that the TF2 has exploded. See attached pictures. The charger presents no errors in SCB.
We have turned off the chargers power. Dont know what has caused this. Even the lock on the door is damaged. Want to know if this is a warranty case before we start to change parts on it.
Cant see anything else then TF2, BC1, BC2 and the lock on the door that is affected.
Root cause:
Solution: Query addressed, please see the latest email from ES team.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0362414-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P9 170001020] TF2 exploded CRM:00643000674
additional_info.body:
Good morning Magnus,
I am reaching out regarding ticket
ID0362414
about charger
rMaRUd
with exploded TF2 component. Thank you for sharing the pictures!
Regarding the warranty case, I see from ISP assets that the charger reports as delivery date 9/8/2022, therefore the charger is still under warranty.
Before proceeding with the investigation from our side, in order to determine which components have been damaged and needs to be replaced and to understand what was the source of this failure, I need some more information from your side:
When did the technician go onsite and notice the damaged charger? Was the onsite activity planned to replace any component or for any faulty behavior on the charger?
You said that the charger reported no errors in SCB. Can you please tell me when did you check this? So for me to have a reference timestamp.
I see from pictures that IMDs and BT2 are severely damaged, so I am confused as I would expect at least to have the outlets OoO. Were the outlets OoO?
Was any replacement activity or onsite investigation done in the same charger area (F05 or F04) lately? Was any work done lately on Voltage transducers, contactors, benders?
If yes, can you please share with me the activity reports?
Do you know if the charger performed charging sessions before the onsite visit? Were reported any charging sessions with errors lately?
Did the technician notice any damages on PLC I/O KF4 and KF7? If yes, do you have pictures of them?
Did the technician notice any damages on connectors XD10.3A and XD10.3B? If yes, do you have pictures of them?
Do you have pictures of the DC2 plus and minus copper bars WC26 and WC27, where TF2 and BC2 are connected?
Did any converter show signs of damage?
Thank you in advance for the feedback to my questions!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: Sv: 0362414 - ID0362414-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P9 170001020] TF2 exploded CRM:00472000232
additional_info.body:
Good morning Magnus,
I am sending you a report email after our call today.
I analyzed the logs from failed sessions on 24.10, after booting up following the replacement of damaged components.
The logs show that charging sessions fail, on both outlets, with pilot state going from A→B2 and with EcoG error “PLC link no SLAC” or “no PLC link”. From the logs, we also see no modbus communication happening between SECC and PLC, as the Charging Phase does not change. No EVMAC is also detected.
By remotely connecting via ssh to the EcoG, I simulated a charging session on the EcoG webUI via the “connect emulated EV” button. After this simulation, I can see in the logs a correct communication between SECC and PLC, as per picture below:
I performed this simulation both on the EcoG-main (DC2) and EcoG-LE (DC1), with the same positive outcome.
In conclusion, it seems to me that the State Monitor is not functioning properly, as it seems unable to communicate with the vehicle. Therefore, please order a new state monitor and proceed with the replacement. Considering that the charger is located in a remote area, I would suggest you to bring onsite also an EcoG-Main and EcoG-LE, just in case to have spare parts, even though from the simulations they seem to work fine.
We will align in the next days so to plan the replacement activity and test session.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: Sv: 0362414 - ID0362414-DC/Si-D/SE [MP / P9 170001020] TF2 exploded CRM:00472000232
additional_info.body:
Good evening Magnus,
Today we finally managed to solve all the issues and to bring the charger
rMaRUd
back to its operation!
During today's onsite activity, the state monitor KF13 was replaced, as indicated in my previous email below. After the replacement, DC1 performed successful charging sessions, but DC2 was not able to charge. Here follows a summary of the findings and actions performed:
From the logs of attempted charging sessions with DC2, I could see that the charging session was failing during cable check. The pilot state went from B2 > C2, the command to the contactors QA13-14 was “on” state, but the feedback from contactors was always on “off” state. The session then ended with error code 67, which is how the EcoG interprets the failure during CableCheck. By checking the EcoG logs, I could see how the voltage was not build up during CableCheck.
Because the “command:on” is just an input from the PLC to the State Monitor to close the contactors, it does not mean that the contactors actually receive the 24V signal to close. We then proceeded to check if the issue was on the command side or on the feedback side.
It was measured during Cable check the presence of the 24V signal “command:on” coming from the state monitor in the terminal F03-XD10.3B cable 6. Measurement was 0V (point 1).
It was measured the signal from PLC KF2 to State Monitor. During Cable check, 24V arrived to the state monitor (point 2).
Because the CP signal is correctly detected and modulated by the EcoG main KF11 (from logs and EcoG webUI), we checked that the CP signal was reaching the State Monitor. The measurement on CCS-B IN (J5) CP was corrcetly12V when in Pilot State “A”.
Finally, the dip-switches of the state monitor were checked and it was found that the dip-switches of DC2 were in a wrong configuration.
Once the correct configuration of the dip-switches was restored, the charger successfully performed charging sessions on outlet DC2.
Thank you again for your collaboration and support!
I will proceed to close this ticket as the issue is finally solved.
